young.what: You have two bean-shaped kidneys near your back, just above your waist.
young.does: They clean your blood and make wee (urine) from the waste and extra water.
young.funFact: Each kidney is about the size of your fist!

junior.what: The kidneys are a pair of bean-shaped organs at the back of the abdomen, one on each side of the spine.
junior.does: They filter the blood, removing wastes such as urea along with extra water and salts to make urine. They also help control blood pressure.
junior.funFact: Each kidney contains about a million tiny filters called nephrons.
junior.details: All of your blood passes through your kidneys many times every day.

junior.what: The ureters are two thin, muscular tubes, one running from each kidney down to the bladder.
junior.does: Waves of muscle contraction push urine down from the kidneys into the bladder.
junior.funFact: Each ureter is about 25–30 cm long.
junior.details: Urine trickles down the ureters all the time, a few drops every few seconds.

young.what: Your bladder is a stretchy bag low down in your tummy.
young.does: It stores wee until you are ready to go to the toilet.
young.funFact: It stretches like a balloon as it fills up!

junior.what: The urinary bladder is a hollow, muscular bag in the lower pelvis.
junior.does: It stores urine and squeezes it out through the urethra. Nerves in its wall tell the brain when it is getting full.
junior.funFact: An adult bladder can comfortably hold about 400–500 mL of urine.
junior.details: Rings of muscle called sphincters keep the bladder closed until you decide to empty it.
